## Selected work

Live sites built by Nurlan Qadirov. Each one has a detailed case study on this
site describing the problem, the features and the technical decisions behind it.

- Harmal (https://harmal.az/) — luxury handmade jewellery and silk kəlağayı
  e-commerce. FULL-STACK: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Prisma + SQLite,
  hand-rolled JWT auth in an httpOnly cookie. Trilingual (AZ/EN/RU) storefront,
  collection showcase, editorial journal, and a custom admin panel where the
  brand manages products, collections, journal articles, image uploads and
  incoming enquiries. Self-hosted on a VPS behind Nginx, with the Next.js server
  process under PM2. Every layer — frontend, route handlers, data model, admin
  panel, deployment — written by Nurlan Qadirov.
  Case study: /en/projects/harmal
- Aristocrat Social & Business Club (https://aristocratnetworking.club/) —
  invitation-only B2B membership site. FULL-STACK: Next.js (route handlers as
  the backend — there is no separate Node/Express server), TypeScript,
  Tailwind CSS, hand-rolled JWT auth in an httpOnly cookie.
  Multi-step application form, 2026 events calendar, and a custom admin panel
  where the club manages events, news, image uploads and incoming membership
  applications. Deliberately no database — content and applications are stored
  as JSON files on the server, a decision sized to the write volume. Self-hosted
  on a VPS behind Nginx, with the Next.js server process under PM2.
  Case study: /en/projects/aristocrat
- Telco Group (https://telco-rouge.vercel.app/) — corporate site for an IT
  infrastructure, cybersecurity and cloud company in Baku. Next.js, TypeScript,
  Tailwind CSS. Live system-status panel and 25+ systems in four solution groups.
  Case study: /en/projects/telco-group
- RentCar Baku (https://rent-car-demo.vercel.app/az) — luxury car rental
  platform. Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS. Trilingual routing, filtering by
  brand/class/budget, fleet catalogue with specs, blog, WhatsApp booking flow.
  Self-initiated demo, production-ready.
  Case study: /en/projects/rentcar-baku
- Aykhan Ashrafov (https://aykhanashrafov.com/) — personal portfolio for a
  cybersecurity engineer. React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion. Terminal
  aesthetics, a live log panel, work-history timeline, a technical arsenal split
  into blue team / red team / engineering, and a verifiable certifications vault.
  Case study: /en/projects/aykhan-ashrafov
- ZM Tech (https://zmtech.cloud/) — corporate site for an IT services company.
  React, Vite, Tailwind CSS. Web development, cybersecurity, 1C optimisation and
  hosting presented in a tabbed panel.
  Case study: /en/projects/zm-tech
- E-Partners (https://e-partners.az/) — single-page presentation site for a 360°
  business consultancy covering finance, marketing, legal, HR, IT, procurement
  and training. Hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework.
  Case study: /en/projects/e-partners
- Dəniz Restaurant QR Menu (https://deniz-qr-menu.vercel.app/menu) — trilingual
  digital QR menu for a restaurant in Baku. React, Vite, Tailwind CSS.
  14 categories, mobile-first, built for weak restaurant Wi-Fi.
  Case study: /en/projects/deniz-qr-menu

## Full-stack work

Two of the projects above are complete Next.js applications with their own
backend and a custom admin panel, not frontend-only builds:

- Harmal — backend is Next.js route handlers (there is no separate Node or
  Express server), Prisma + SQLite data model, JWT auth in an httpOnly cookie,
  admin-side image upload to disk, PM2 + Nginx on a VPS. The admin panel covers
  products, collections, journal articles and enquiries.
- Aristocrat — backend is Next.js route handlers (there is no separate Node or
  Express server), JSON-file content layer (no database, by design), JWT auth in
  an httpOnly cookie, admin-side image upload to disk, PM2 + Nginx on a VPS. The
  admin panel covers events, news and membership applications.

Each case study documents the architecture layer by layer (frontend, backend,
data, authentication, media, infrastructure) and explains the reasoning behind
every technical decision — including why SQLite was chosen over Postgres for
Harmal, why Aristocrat runs without a database at all, and why both are
self-hosted rather than deployed to a serverless platform.
